newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates ease on fresh fund injection.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates ease on fresh fund injection.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady to slightly lower as Bank Negara continued to inject funds into the system, dealers said on Thursday.
They said Bank Negara was said to have come in directly and lent to discount houses. Its agent banks were also lending one-month money, they added.
No confirmation was available from Bank Negara, which does not comment on its open market operations.
"I believe some discount houses directly got funds from Negara, but we cannot confirm it," said a local bank dealer.
At 0430 GMT, one-month money was at 7.8/8.0 percent against 8.0, three-month was at 7.8/8.0 percent against 7.9/8.1 and six-month at 7.8/8.0 percent against 8.0 percent.
Bank Negara is said to have injected funds over the past week to help ease market tightness.
Recent heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank to defend the currency from speculative attack had caused a liquidity squeeze.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were up across the board, reflecting the fall in interest rates, futures dealers said.
At 0450 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up four at 92.42, or an implied yield of 7.58 percent.
The December contract was up three at 92.63, or 7.57 percent.
